prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one objectively “best” roofer for Denver (best depends on your neighborhood, roof type, whether you want help with insurance, timing and budget). I can, however, give a practical way to find the best roofer for your hail damage and help you vet contenders.

Quick plan
1. Narrow candidates: get 3 estimates from roofers who advertise storm/hail damage work and have good local reviews. Use Google/Angi/Yelp/BBB/Nextdoor and the shingle manufacturers’ certified contractor lookup (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed).
2. Vet them: check licensing, insurance, warranties, manufacturer certifications, local references, and BBB rating.
3. Compare bids: scope of work, materials, photos of damage, roof life expectancy, deductible handling, timeline, and written warranty.
4. Decide and monitor the job.

What to look for (must-haves)
- Colorado contractor license (verify locally if applicable) and current insurance (general liability + workers’ comp). Ask for a certificate of insurance.
- Manufacturer certification (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, or CertainTeed Select); these matter for long-term warranty.
- Experience with hail claims and storm teams in Denver — they should be familiar with local insurance processes.
- Written estimate with itemized materials, labor, tear-off vs. overlay, and warranties (material and workmanship).
- Local references and recent photos of similar completed jobs.

Questions to ask each roofer
- How many hail-damage jobs have you done in the last 12 months?
- Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers? Which?
- Will you handle insurance communications/meetings with the adjuster?
- Do you pull permits and coordinate inspections?
- What is your warranty (workmanship and materials)?
- Do you subcontract? If so, who will supervise?

Red flags
- Door-to-door storm-chaser offers “today only” discounts or asks for full payment up-front.
- No local address, poor or no reviews, or no proof of insurance.
- Pressure to sign before you get multiple bids or before the adjuster inspects.
- Estimates that are non-itemized, very low compared to others, or vague on materials.

Insurance tips
- File a claim promptly if damage is severe. Keep photos and records.
- Get multiple estimates before accepting a payout.
- If the insurer’s adjuster misses damage, a reputable roofer should be able to document and discuss with the adjuster or recommend a public adjuster.

Ballpark cost & timeline (Denver, rough)
- Minor repairs: a few hundred to a few thousand dollars.
- Full asphalt shingle replacement for a typical home: often a few thousand to $10–20k depending on size and materials.
- Timeline: expect estimates within a week or two, scheduling within 1–6 weeks depending on season and storm volume.

How I can help right now
- If you tell me your neighborhood or zip code I can tell you what to search for and what to ask locally, or
- Paste 2–3 written estimates and I’ll compare them line-by-line and point out concerning items, or
- I can draft a short phone/email script you can use to contact roofers and ask the right questions.

Which would you prefer?
